name: What every community board asked the City for
blurb: Every community board's Capital and Expense Budget Requests since 2019 with the agency's response to each, combined from NYC Open Data and the Register PDFs. Click a district on the map, compare its requests against its 311 complaint categories, and draft a follow-up email to the agency.

name: Where Medicaid hurts, in New Yorkers' own words
blurb: A radar for the NYS Office of Customer Experience: the biggest problems people hit with Medicaid, laid out in the order they move through the program, sized by people affected and shaded by online mentions, with public YouTube stories for each. Sample data for the demo.

name: Where to put a city grocery store
blurb: Identifies disadvantaged census tracts with high food insecurity and strong transit connectivity, then scores vacant city-owned lots as candidate store sites. Adjust the scoring weights and the top sites re-rank live.

name: Answer a City summons
blurb: A plain-language guide for business owners who received a City summons: pick the issuing agency, enter the dates on the ticket, and see your deadlines and all four response options explained.

name: Get affordable housing approved
blurb: Pick one of three real Brooklyn affordable-housing projects, set the financing and site facts, and get a phased roadmap of every approval between you and lease-up, including the ones the subsidy itself triggers.

name: Flood risk against flood spending
blurb: An interactive dashboard connecting where New York floods to where the city spends its flood-resilience capital dollars, down to the community-district level, plus a time-animated playback of the May 20 flash flood across the subway and bus network.
builders: David A. Lee, Dean Berkowitz & Lyndsey Kaplan

name: A game that teaches 311
blurb: A video game that teaches New Yorkers how to use 311, turning the city's main service request line into something residents can actually navigate.

name: Procurement record search
blurb: A tool for searching and reviewing city procurement records, making contracting data legible to anyone who needs to follow where public money goes.

name: Live transit data for AI tools
blurb: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling live investigation of transit reliability. Already past 1,000 downloads since the event.

name: Index of NYC's public datasets
blurb: A website that indexes NYC's civic data, giving residents and builders one place to find the datasets the city publishes.

name: Map of NYC business health
blurb: A map of the health of NYC businesses, surfacing where the local economy is thriving or under stress across the city.

name: Find open city bids
blurb: A tool for finding and tracking open NYC government bid and procurement opportunities, helping vendors see where they can compete for city work.

name: Fill benefits forms by voice
blurb: A voice assistant that lets New Yorkers fill out their benefits forms by talking through them, instead of navigating the application themselves.
